`143-146`: ** Major** · **Performance & Scalability** · **Heavy lift** ⚠️ **Unverified finding** Verification ran but could not confirm this finding. It is shown for review, not as a verified issue. **Probe only new stream data. Re-probing the full buffer on every read takes quadratic CPU time and blocks the event loop.** `stageResponse` appends each chunk to `text` and then calls `probe(text, format)` on the whole buffer. For SSE, `proxx.budget.stream/probe` splits every buffered line again. It then runs `JSON.parse` and `js->clj :keywordize-keys true` on every `data:` event again and replays `consume` from the empty state. Total work therefore grows with N²/2 for N events before readiness. Trigger: a managed Gemma stream emits only `reasoning_content` events until the 12 s free cutoff. The 20 s paid deadline allows the same on the paid route. At about 50–100 tokens/s, often one event per chunk, that is about 600–1200 events. It means about 180k–720k CLJS parse/convert operations per attempt. That work is synchronous on the Node event loop, so it delays every concurrent request in the proxy. Visible-content streams become ready early and avoid the cost. Reasoning-first streams are the case this PR targets (see the "reasoning-only free stream" regression). Fix: make the probe incremental. - Keep a byte or line offset in `stageResponse`. - Pass only new complete lines to the probe, plus the prior probe state (accumulated `tools`, `ready`, `fatal`). - Have `probe` accept and return that state. The CLJS function stays pure; it only stops rescanning. - Keep `JSON` format probing at end-of-body only. A partial JSON body cannot parse anyway.
